subject: Programmatic access to problems encountered when running variational Bayes

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Programmatic access to problems encountered when running variational Bayes
parts: On a recent manual run of rstan::vb() the text output to the console included several warning messages ("may be diverging," "algorithm may not have converged"). However, none of these were actual R warnings, and I could find no hint in the stanfit object returned that there had been any possible problem. I have a use case where I'm doing a large number of rstan::vb() runs, and it's not really feasible to have a human eyeball all of the console output. Is there any way to get programmatic access to any such indicators of possible problems?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Programmatic access to problems encountered when running variational Bayes
parts:
On Monday, April 25, 2016 at 12:09:57 PM UTC-4, Kevin Van Horn wrote:
Is there any way to get programmatic access to any such indicators of possible problems?

No, the C++ code for ADVI doesn't return the same stuff as MCMC. You can get it to print a diagnostic file, but there is no code in RStan to read it. At best, you could divert stdout to a file and parse it yourself, but I would be worried about running ADVI in an automated setting.

Ben
